A fetch installs its tracking ref when that ref still has the commit the fetch observed, or when the fetched commit descends from the current tracking commit. A slower fetch does not move the ref back to an older commit.
A file remote fetch, pull, or clone reads committed refs without the remote graph lock, so it succeeds while another connection holds a write transaction on that database.
A branch push takes the local graph lock, and refuses a read-only connection, before changing the remote. Deleting a remote branch with no local tracking ref still reports success.

Fetch and pull stage downloaded chunks without the local graph lock, and take that lock only to commit a pending batch and to install tracking refs. A download that fails first leaves those refs unchanged.
